entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Shibli Nomani was an Indian Islamic scholar, poet, philosopher, historian, educational thinker, author, orator, reformer and critic of orientalists during the British Raj. He is regarded as the father of Urdu historiography. He was also proficient in Arabic and Persian languages. Shibli was associated with two influential movements in the region, the Aligarh and the Nadwa movements.

As a supporter of the Deobandi school, he believed that English language and European sciences should be incorporated into the education system. Shibli Nomani was a philosophers & thinkers from Azamgarh (1857-06-03, Azamgarh–1914-11-18). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Shibli Nomani's work on Urdu historiography had a significant impact on the region, shaping the narrative of Indian history and influencing educational reforms. His incorporation of European sciences into the education system also contributed to the growth of modern Islamic scholarship.
